rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. `python.defaultInterpreterPath` does not translate an explicit Unix-style executable path into a Windows executable path. For shared workspace settings, use `"python.defaultInterpreterPath": "${workspaceFolder}/.venv"` instead: the documented directory form supports the environment layout appropriate to each operating system (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/python/settings-reference). This setting supplies the initial default only; if an interpreter has already been selected for the workspace, use **Python: Select Interpreter** (`python.setInterpreter`) to choose `.venv/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows. Closing this as intended behavior rather than a path-conversion bug.

Per-subfolder pytest invocation is already supported through multi-project testing: install the Python Environments extension, enable it with "python.useEnvironmentsExtension": true, and configure packages/api and packages/core as Python projects. Leave python.testing.cwd unset so each pytest invocation starts in its own project directory and can load that package's pytest.ini or pyproject.toml configuration. Without this integration, testing falls back to one workspace-wide root. The supported workflow is documented at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/wiki/Multi%E2%80%90Project-Testing-in-VS-Code, so this request can be closed as covered by the existing capability.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report. The earlier fix in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/pull/24319 guards Pixi enumeration, but the legacy locator still initializes its watcher separately and warns when .pixi/envs is absent. This remains a logging improvement for the environments area; the missing optional directory should not suggest a configuration problem in a non-Pixi workspace.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and discussion. The testing-output design has since moved toward the integrated Test Results panel, and the remaining work to correlate stdout, stderr, and logs with each test is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/issues/22594. That work covers the requested single-click path from a test to its readable output; the requirement to navigate directly to the selected test's output should be preserved there, so I suggest consolidating on that issue.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the same capability: clicking a test surfaces that test's own pytest output; B implements per-test output correlation shown in the Test Results panel on click, delivering A's ask.

rows.title: "Run tests at cursor" takes exponentially longer with more pytest tests
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and detailed reproduction. This was fixed in VS Code core by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6ab3a15691ff9a1aa619a53d9dcd29c0b53d76a1 via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/219809: gutter-triggered test runs now coalesce parameterized children into their runnable parent instead of including every child individually. This can be closed as completed.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff collapses each individually-passed child test into its parent before running gutter/cursor test actions, removing the per-parametrized-case explosion the report measured as super-linear slowdown.

rows.title: Python REPL should use a snake icon
Test Discovery Failing in all repos (for the Testing Panel)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and detailed logs. The Unix-domain-socket communication causing these permission failures was replaced with FIFO-based communication for Linux and macOS in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/commit/d1d125a6cd7201883503da173bd774b1809b5a0e via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/pull/24343, and the change shipped in 2024.22.0. Current releases no longer use the failing UDS path for test discovery, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in v2024.22.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The reported failure is net.createServer listen EACCES on a Unix-domain socket in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; the diff removes that socket-binding path on linux/mac entirely, replacing it with mkfifo plus chmod 0666 FIFOs.

rows.title: Cwd choice for repl in multi root workspaces locks in choice
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/commit/3275c34acfa9be393e0239769e7e587e94db477a and shipped in 2025.6.0. Closing the native REPL now clears the cached session, so opening a new one in a multi-root workspace runs the working-directory selector again. The fix shipped in v2025.6.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: On REPL notebook close the diff clears the cached singleton (nativeRepl = undefined) and disposes server/controller, so reopening reconstructs the REPL and re-runs the folder quick pick the report says never reappears.

rows.title: `Start native repl` always opens repl to side even if there is nothing open
Code coverage breaks when "relative paths" is enabled
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/commit/cd714bf25cde196854d7e78e8e0c20be54edaf55 and shipped in 2025.6.0: relative coverage filenames are now converted to absolute paths before they are sent to VS Code, so file navigation and gutter coverage use valid paths. I believe this is resolved on current releases. The fix shipped in v2025.6.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff resolves non-absolute coverage file keys to absolute paths before building the coverage map, exactly the relative_files=true mechanism the report blames for invalid paths and missing gutters.

rows.title: Unable to select Interpreter because special characters in the windows username.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the concrete Windows trace. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/issues/24126, which tracks shell-aware escaping for generated Python commands. This report adds an important cmd.exe case: the interpreter-validation command consumes the carets in `C:\Users\^_^\...`, changing the path to `C:\Users\_\...`; that detail should be retained with the canonical issue as the work is consolidated there.
rows.verifyEvidence: B scopes itself to non-Windows shells mis-quoting paths with double quotes; A is Windows cmd stripping carets from unquoted interpreter-script arguments — a different platform and escaping defect, so closing A loses the Windows case.

rows.title: Shell Integration makes REPL prompt garbled
Enable PyREPL for 3.13 and above
Avoid loading `sys` and `platform` modules into namespace when running PYTHONSTARTUP in integrated terminal
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This cleanup is still needed on current main: `pythonrc.py` executes in the interactive namespace and leaves its imported modules and helpers there. The suggested `del` statements cannot be applied directly because the prompt hooks continue looking up `sys` and `readline` after startup; the implementation should instead preserve those dependencies outside the user's namespace. The related work in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/pull/26045 should be considered when scoping the change.
